notes: Summary: Kestrel runs a high-concurrency customer-facing travel chat (booking + itinerary summarization). Looking for Dedicated capacity to guarantee throughput during campaign spikes and to keep latency tight for booking flows.

Traffic profile (from sample week): steady-state QPS approx 12 req/s; daily peaks driven by promotional blasts up to ~110–130 QPS for 10–20 minute windows; taily burstiness with 95th percentile spikes ~2.5x baseline.
Request composition: 60% retrieval+rerank then 40% decoder generation. Average decode tokens per request ~300 tokens (median 220, 95th 760). Average embed calls per session: 3.
- Steady-state: target capacity to handle 12 QPS generation concurrently with p95 latency target; token/sec steady = 12 * 300 = 3,600 tokens/sec.
- Peak burst: plan for 120 QPS sustained for 15 minutes (capacity buffer), peak token/sec = 120 * 300 = 36,000 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency model: recommend continuous batching + prefix KV cache for 60% of requests (cache hit expectation ~45%) to reduce duplicate compute during sessions.

GPU recommendation (initial): reserve 8 x A100-80GB equivalent for steady-state (expected to meet p95 latency with batching and KV caching). Add burst pool of 24 GPUs (A100/H100 mix) for peak windows and campaign days. Consider H100s for heavy long-context experiments.

Latency SLO targets discussed: p50 < 60ms (non-streaming prompt routing), p95 < 220ms for end-to-end generation (with streaming enabled where possible). Kestrel emphasized that booking-confirmation flows must land under p95 SLA reliably.

SLA asks from Kestrel: 99.95% availability, p95 latency guarantee with crediting for violations, 4-hour P1 response + 24-hour remediation calendar. Legal wants concrete MTTR and credit formula — SE/AE to propose language.
Cost sensitivity: target effective inference cost per 1M tokens < $2,500 after batching/caching improvements — aggressive but necessary to justify Dedicated commit vs hosted mix.

Model & routing preferences: prefer Redmond-v2 style open decoder for cheaper operations; fallback to smaller quantized variant during capacity pressure; multi-model routing by policy (latency-first for checkout, cost-first for async tasks).

Security/ops: must support customer-managed KMS, VPC peering (no public egress for EU customers), audit logs retained 3 years, SAML SSO into console. On-prem option required for a subset of regulated EU bookings.
